issue_request: FHIR-6975 was a Published FHIR-core terminology-service change request with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. It reported that the DSTU1 terminology-service ValueSet validation example used `$validate`, proposed changing the example to POST `$validate-code`, and was resolved with the decision that GET is allowed but the operation name should be fixed.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-6975. Git history shows d0cb9bccebc2b8b01ffd9a79bef65e120fd230c3 changed the terminology-service example from GET `$validate` to GET `$validate-code` on 2015-06-18, preserving GET. Commit cfcf4590696ecabe6964951fc1eb96205920ee77 later added the ValueSet `$validate-code` request example file with GET and POST examples.
additional_context: The current build hierarchy includes `source/terminology-service.html`. The current terminology-service page, ValueSet operation request example, and ValueSet OperationDefinition consistently use `ValueSet-validate-code`; the OperationDefinition has `affectsState=false` and supports type and instance invocation, consistent with a side-effect-free GET example. The Jira text's unprefixed legacy "Track# 5531" is not the modern FHIR-5531 Jira issue, which is an unrelated Patient search issue.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current authoritative source already has the corrected `$validate-code` operation name and retains the GET example exactly as permitted by the final resolution.
